newsitem.title: GERMANY: Hypo-Bank shares surge on takeover talk.
newsitem.headline: Hypo-Bank shares surge on takeover talk.

text.p: Shares in Hypo-Bank AG, Germany's fifth largest commercial bank and a specialist in mortgage lending, surged on Wednesday as dealers said takeover rumours surrounding the bank had intensified.

Shares in Hypo-Bank leapt 2.80 marks, more than five percent, to 57.80 on the IBIS electronic bourse as dealers said Dresdner Bank AG, the second largest in the sector, was being mooted as interested in a takeover.
A Dresdner spokesman said it was making no comment on the market rumours and a spokesman for Hypo-Bank said it had had no notification of any stake in it held by Dresdner.
Hypo-Bank's full name is Bayerische Hypotheken- und Wechsel-Bank AG.

Dealers said earlier that takeover rumours in the banking sector, a constant feature of market trading in the latter half of last year, had resurfaced in the light of the Krupp-Thyssen takeover bid, which although now dropped in favour of a joint venture plan, had rekindled market interest in merger activity.
Other banking shares were also higher, with Deutsche Bank AG traded 93 marks or 2.4 percent higher at 93.67 marks at bourse close and Dresdner Bank itself up 1.45 marks at 59.25.
